study_identification_part.si_4_title: Comprehensive volumetric phenotyping of the neonatal brain in Down syndrome

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Two datasets were used: (1) developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP) - an open-access project providing preterm- to term-born control neonates for normative modeling; (2) Early Brain Imaging in DS (eBiDS) study - a single-site clinical research cohort at St Thomas' Hospital/Evelina Children's Hospital, London, providing neonates with Down syndrome. Note: dHCP is classified as HCP-D (Human Connectome Project Development) as it focuses on the developing human brain. The eBiDS is classified as SINGLE-SITE as it is a single institutional cohort without a standardized dataset name.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: "A total of 493 preterm- to term-born neonates [...] were selected from the dHCP (www.developingconnectome.org) [...] for normative modeling of brain tissue volumes from 32 to 46 weeks PMA at scan."; "Neonates with a postnatally confirmed karyotype for DS were recruited from the neonatal unit and postnatal wards at St Thomas' Hospital London and invited for a neonatal scan"; "The dHCP is an open-access project. The imaging data used in this study were included in the third dHCP data release (2021)"
